subject: general
question: Which of the following compounds is used in a soda-acid fire extinguisher?
solution:
The correct answer is __**NaHCO3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **NaHCO3** is commonly known as **sodium bicarbonate** or **baking soda**.
 
• In a **soda-acid fire extinguisher**, sodium bicarbonate reacts with sulfuric acid to produce carbon dioxide gas.
 
• The **carbon dioxide** gas produced helps to smother the fire by cutting off the **oxygen supply**.
 
• This reaction also produces water, which helps in cooling the fire.
 
• Sodium bicarbonate is preferred due to its **easy availability**, **cost-effectiveness**, and **non-toxic nature**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Na2CO3**__

 __
 
• **Sodium carbonate**, also known as **soda ash** or **washing soda**, is not used in fire extinguishers.
 
• It is primarily used in **glass manufacturing** and as a **cleaning agent**.
 
 
 
• **H2CO3**__
 __
 
• **Carbonic acid** is a weak acid formed when **carbon dioxide dissolves in water**.
 
• It is not used in fire extinguishers and is primarily found in **carbonated beverages**.
 
 
 
• **Ca(OH)2**__
 
 
• **Calcium hydroxide**, also known as **slaked lime** or **hydrated lime**, is not suitable for fire extinguishers.
 
• It is commonly used in **construction**, **water treatment**, and **agriculture**.
